instructions: Finely chop the onion, carrots and celery. Drain and rinse both cans of beans, then mash one can in a bowl with a fork until mostly smooth.
Heat 3 tbsp of the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery with 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and lightly golden.
Meanwhile, strip the leaves from 1 sprig of rosemary and chop them finely. Chop 4 sage leaves. Mince the garlic.
Add the rosemary, sage, garlic and tomato paste to the pot. Stir for 1 minute, until the paste turns a shade darker.
Add the broth, the mashed beans, the whole beans, the farro and 1 tsp salt. Stir well and bring it to a boil.

Turn the heat down to medium-low and simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, stirring every few minutes. It's ready when the farro is tender but still a little chewy and the soup is thick. If it gets too thick, stir in a splash of water.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle into bowls. Drizzle each bowl with some of the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and add a grind of pepper.
method_notes: No page for this dish by name has 20 ratings, so this is a fallback. The soup's core is farro cooked in a bean base, soffritto of onion, carrot and celery, rosemary and sage. Italy Magazine purees the beans and adds tomato concentrate; Just a Pinch uses canned borlotti beans and semi-pearled farro at 1 cup to about 3 cups of liquid, which this follows, with extra broth for a dinner-sized soup. SBS and Italy Magazine include pancetta or dried soaked beans taking over an hour; this drops the pancetta (vegan) and uses canned beans to fit the time. Mashing one can of beans is the quick stand-in for the purée.
